title: Study about pre-operative use of qigong-based practices and their effects on the perioperative course during surgical interventions in the upper GI-tract.
summary:
The study investigates the effect of preoperative Qigong-based mindfulness exercises on body weight as part of the preparation for bariatric surgery, in addition to the standard intervention. The aim is to evaluate their impact on weight, medication requirements, postoperative pain, and recovery.
Two groups will be compared: a standard intervention group and a Qigong group. Data collection includes pain intensity, medication consumption, biomarkers, vital signs, and quality of life, across a total of seven visits, including three postoperative follow-ups at 1, 2, and 30 days.
The results are intended to contribute to the optimization of standard care and to support the integration of complementary medical approaches into routine perioperative clinical management.

interventions.name: Group A with Standard-Care: receives the usual multimodal concept containing nutritional-, movement- and behavioral therapy, which starts six months prior to bariatric surgery.

Group B: additional to the standard care, these patients get regular qigong based interventions. First four weeks once weekly, then once monthly until the planned operation.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients aged ≥18 years
Planned bariatric surgery within a multimodal treatment program
Sufficient communication skills and proficiency in German (or English, if applicable)
Exclusion criteria:
1.Regular participation in mindfulness-based movement therapies such as Tai Chi, yoga, or comparable practices within the past 6 months
2.Relevant psychiatric disorders (e.g., borderline personality disorder with risk of self-harm, moderate to severe depression, post-traumatic stress disorder)
3.Neurological conditions (e.g., history of stroke, polyneuropathy)
4.Limited physical mobility preventing participation in light exercise
5.Cognitive impairment or language barriers that interfere with understanding the exercises or instructions
6.Chronic pain syndromes requiring ongoing significant pharmacological treatment
7.Current relevant substance abuse (e.g., alcohol, opioids)
